title: Gurage Enset Bulla
community: Gurage and enset-eating communities of southern Ethiopia
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Gurage Bulla — the liquid extracted from the enset (false banana) root starch, cooked into a smooth, white porridge with kibbeh and honey. The most distinctive Gurage food after kitfo — the enset starch produces a porridge unlike any grain-based alternative.
longDesc: Bulla is the purest expression of the enset food tradition — the white starch extracted from the enset root, cooked into a porridge that is simultaneously filling and digestible. Given to sick people, children, and pregnant women in the Gurage tradition.
ingredients: 1 cup enset starch (bulla) — or substitute arrowroot starch
steps: Whisk starch with 1 cup cold water.
Bring remaining water to a simmer.
Cook stirring 12—15 minutes until smooth and thick.
Serve with kibbeh and honey in the centre.
chefTips: Authentic bulla starch from the enset plant is white and very fine — unlike any grain starch.
cookingScience: Enset starch gelatinises at a lower temperature than most grain starches — producing a smoother, more delicate porridge.
sustainabilityTips: Enset is one of the world's most remarkable famine-resistant plants — it grows in very poor soil and difficult conditions.
culturalNote: Bulla is the food of Gurage care — given to newborn babies when solid food is introduced, to sick family members, and to pregnant women. The white, smooth porridge of enset starch is the Gurage version of chicken soup.
